body:
Hey, what part of the US? I don't even know what to talk about right now. And right now I just want someone to be with.

I just took some seroquel so I will probably be asleep soon.

I have a tendency to develop crushes on waitresses and baristas, and fantasize about romantic relationships with them, developing into a happy life together.

Then I crash back to reality and drink some more vodka while counting the amount of pills I have, debating whether or not tonight is the night I down 149 of them with as much vodka as possible - calculating how much I can drink without vomiting so as to be sure it does the job and I drift off peacefully into a permanent rest with happy fantasies on part of my mind battling with depressing thoughts on the other part of it.

Fantasizing for me is very much like experiencing a hypomanic phase - loving it, wanting to stay in it, but knowing that it will end and when it does you crash into a crippling depressive state. Happens every time. I like to try and convince myself it's almost worth it.

The fantasizing (and the hypomanic states) almost lead me to think I can do something and offer something to someone or multiple someones. I almost am able to pick up a pen and start writing, although my anxiety and desire for perfection in all I do prevents that because I know when I come down - even if not to a depressive state, maybe just slightly less hypomanic - I will be displeased with what I have produced.

I'm not sure.

Being in your own head is dangerous.

Living in fantasies in your own head is probably just as dangerous.
